findings.title: Residual-offer selection relies on a result-discovery surface that does not exist, and its fallback cannot meet the non-empty-offers criterion
findings.description: T13 tells the implementer to "reuse 320's existing result-discovery surface". If there isn't one, it says to "scope this task to the store-recorded samples only and note the gap". No such surface exists in `src/squadron/metrology/`. The only review-file lookup is `capture.resolve_target` (`src/squadron/metrology/capture.py:95`), which globs `{index}-review.*` for a single index. It cannot list every judge result for a `JudgeConfigId`. Store-recorded samples are by definition already sampled, so the fallback always returns zero offers. That breaks the slice success criterion "a graduated config with unsampled results yields a non-empty offer set" and T14's non-empty test. Lapse detection also needs the current judge results, so it breaks too. The gap can be checked now, so settle it in planning rather than mid-task. Have T13 specify the scan: glob the reviews dir, call `derive_judge_config_id` on each file, drop files already referenced by a `SampleVerdict.result_ref`, and match on the exact `JudgeConfigId`. Name `resolve_store_dir`/the reviews dir as the root, and remove the fallback.

findings.title: Direction-band precedence in T7 contradicts itself
findings.description: The numbered list puts `n < floor → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` first and `TIGHTEN` fourth. The bullets right after it say TIGHTEN must be reachable when `n < floor`. If a junior implementer follows the numbered order, they ship exactly the bug T8 tests for. Rewrite the list in its real order: (1) `match_rate <= tighten_rate` → TIGHTEN, (2) `n < floor` → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, (3) unversioned → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, (4) `match_rate >= graduate_rate` → GRADUATE, (5) HOLD. Also say whether an unversioned cell with a low match rate returns TIGHTEN. Neither the design table nor the task decides this, and T8 should pin it down.

findings.title: Malformed `judge:` block failure mode is neither implemented nor tested
findings.description: The design's Failure Modes table wants a malformed judge block (non-numeric floor) to be "flagged, not silently defaulted", with a WARNING that names the template. `resolve_thresholds` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/judge.py:54-57`) calls `float(...)` on the raw value, so a non-numeric floor raises `ValueError`. It does not fall back. T7 only handles the unregistered-template case, yet its success line says "never raises". The Coverage Check says the malformed case is "exercised in T8", but T8 has no such test. Add a narrow `except ValueError` to T7 that logs a WARNING and marks the target unresolvable or flagged, and add the matching case to T8.

findings.title: The runtime-drawn-model limitation and its `--json` presence are not covered
findings.description: Success criterion 4 requires the runtime-drawn-model limitation (180 pool: the threshold cannot track the drawn model) to be "stated where the recommendation is produced (asserted: the note is present in output, including `--json`)". T9's `model_dimension_note` only covers the "template paired with this model / choose together" text and leaves out the pool limitation. T16 checks that `--json` parses back to the model, but not that the note is non-empty in the JSON. Add the limitation text to T9's note content, and add a T16 assertion that every `cells[*].target.model_dimension_note` in the `--json` output is non-empty.

findings.title: `GraduatedConfig` placement creates a circular import with `models.py`
findings.description: T3 puts `GraduatedConfig` in `calibration_models.py`, and it imports `JudgeConfigId` from `models.py` (`src/squadron/metrology/models.py:67`). T11 then adds `graduated_config: GraduatedConfig | None` to `MetrologyRecord` in `models.py`, so `models.py` must import from `calibration_models.py`. That is a cycle, and in Pydantic it won't survive a plain `TYPE_CHECKING` guard without `model_rebuild`. Decide where the type lives now. The simplest option is to define `GraduatedConfig` (and the `EvidenceSnapshot` it embeds) in `models.py` and re-export it from `calibration_models.py`.

findings.title: Graduate idempotence depends on an update path T11 does not provide
findings.description: T15 requires re-graduating to "update its evidence snapshot in place (one record, not two)". T11's `write_graduation` returns "a generated record id", and the store names files by id (`store.py:100-101`). A second write therefore produces a second file. T11 offers no update or overwrite operation, and `find_graduation` returns a `GraduatedConfig` without its record id. Either derive the record id deterministically from `(JudgeConfigId, artifact_level)` so an atomic overwrite gives idempotence, or have `find_graduation` return the id along with the config. Specify this in T11 so T15 and T16 aren't left to work it out.

findings.title: Pruned-review-file handling is tested in T14 but not specified in T13
findings.description: The failure-mode row "referenced review file gone since graduation → skip, count, WARNING naming the path" appears only as a T14 test bullet. T13's implementation steps and success criteria never mention it, and the return type `list[OfferTarget]` has nowhere to put a count. The lapse signal has the same problem: T13 leaves open how the lapse is reported ("return enough information (or have the CLI re-derive it …)"). Choose one return shape now, for example a small `OfferSelection` with `offers`, `lapsed`, `exhausted` and `pruned_count`. T14 and T15 can then assert against a concrete contract.

findings.title: Commit markers after every task, including untested implementation
findings.description: All 17 tasks end with a `**Commit:**` marker. Implementation tasks (T1, T3, T5, T7, T9, T11, T13, T15) commit before their tests exist, so commits don't land at tested points. The impl/test split also doubles the task count for an effort-3/5 slice. Merge each implementation task with its test task (T1+T2, T3+T4, …, T15+T16), keeping one commit per merged pair. That gives 8 tested commits plus T17.

findings.title: CLI "no evidence" and "no offers due" lines are only partly specified
findings.description: The design wants `recommend` on an empty store to print a "no evidence" line that still states `floor_applied`, and `offers` to print an explanatory line when an exhausted config has nothing due. T15 only specifies the lapsed-graduation line. Add both lines to T15 and add one assertion each to T16.

findings.title: Config-key defaults and rate consistency are unspecified
findings.description: T5 and T6 say "with defaults" but give no values, and the design doesn't either. A junior implementer would have to make them up. Also nothing checks that `tighten_match_rate < graduate_match_rate` or that the rates fall in [0, 1]. Without that check the bands can overlap silently. State the defaults, and consider one fail-fast check where the keys are read.

findings.title: T2 fixtures assume `_template_content_hash` takes a template object
findings.description: `_template_content_hash(template_name: str)` (`identity.py:298`) looks templates up through `get_template`, so it cannot be called on `ReviewTemplate` fixtures directly. Tell the implementer to patch `squadron.review.templates.get_template`, or register fixture templates, so the hash tests don't stall on this.

findings.title: Hash narrowing sequenced first with both-direction regression coverage
findings.description: T1 and T2 target the right function (`identity.py:298-323`) and leave `derive_result_ref` untouched. The regression is tested through `derive_judge_config_id` in both directions, which matches the design's suggested order and success criterion 7.

findings.title: Version-scoped graduation, no-mutation discipline and graduate refusal are covered
findings.description: `GraduatedConfig` carries the full `JudgeConfigId`, and T12 tests matching on differing hashes. No-mutation byte snapshots appear at both the unit layer (T10) and the CLI layer (T16). The graduate refusal and the record-count check are in T16. The Typer-free core test is present. No NFR is restated, so no load-test or CI-gate task is needed.
